title: Relative reductive groups and central covering terminology
statement: Let $B$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let group schemes mean group objects in schemes over $B$, using the diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme] with fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. A homomorphism $i:N\to G$ is central if for every $B$-scheme $V$ and points $n:V\to N$, $g:V\to G$, one has $i(n)g=gi(n)$. A reductive group scheme over $B$ is one in the sense of [def-sfb-relative-reductive-group] (smooth, affine, finite presentation, reductive geometric fibres in the field sense of [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]); it is reused, not redefined. Define a semisimple group scheme over $B$ to be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism], and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], whose pullback to every geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}k\to B$ is semisimple [def-sfb-semisimple-group-scheme]. Spectra have the meaning of [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Affineness gives quasi-compactness and separatedness, so this is finite presentation. It has simply connected fibres if it has simply connected semisimple geometric fibres in the sense of [def-sfb-relative-reductive-conditions]: every geometric pullback $G_s$ is semisimple and every surjective homomorphism $f:G'\to G_s$ with $G'$ semisimple and finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] central scheme-theoretic kernel is an isomorphism; that recorded predicate is reused, not redefined. A split maximal torus inclusion $i:T\to G$ is closed [def-weil-closed-immersion], has $T\simeq T_{B,r}$ for some $r\geq0$, using [def-sfb-relative-split-torus], and is a maximal torus after every geometric pullback in the sense of [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. A Borel inclusion is a closed subgroup inclusion whose every geometric pullback is a Borel subgroup [def-sfb-borel-subgroup-scheme]. Finally, having a split maximal torus means existence of such a torus inclusion. These are predicates and contain no existence theorem for reductive groups or covers. Rank zero and empty bases are allowed.
